statement: Largest known training run >= 5e27 FLOP (Epoch AI; by 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met. The largest known run at end-2025 was ~5e26 FLOP (a Bloc A model, July 2025), ~10x below threshold. The record rose from ~3.5-3.8e26 (Feb) to ~5e26 (Jul). Frontier compute growth looked slower than the 5x/yr trend because developers moved effort to post-training: one flagship (Aug) used less compute (~5e25) than its predecessor (~3.8e26). Epoch argued this pause was temporary. Late-2025 flagships had no compute estimates.

items.summary: A Bloc A developer released the first model estimated above 1e26 FLOP (~3.5e26), setting a new largest-run record.
items.detail: xAI Grok 3 (released 2025-02-17), Colossus (Memphis). Epoch 'How many AI models will exceed compute thresholds?' (2025-05-30) names it the first >1e26 model.

items.summary: A second Bloc A developer released a model estimated at 3.8e26 FLOP (125-day run), briefly the largest known run.
items.detail: OpenAI GPT-4.5 (2025-02-27); Epoch model page 3.8e26 FLOP.

items.summary: The first Bloc A developer released a new record run, which a compute tracker later estimated at ~5e26 FLOP ('the largest AI training run to date'), costing ~$490M and ~310 GWh. The largest known run at end-2025 stood ~10x below the 5e27 threshold.
items.detail: xAI Grok 4 (2025-07-09); Epoch Data Insight 'What did it take to train Grok 4?' (2025-09-12; data updated 2025-11-17).

items.summary: A compute tracker estimated a new Bloc A flagship (Aug 2025) used ~5e25 FLOP in total, likely less than its predecessor's >1e26. This was the first GPT-series flagship to shrink in compute, because training effort shifted to reinforcement-learning post-training.
items.detail: Epoch AI 'Notes on GPT-5 training compute' (Substack/X thread, ~2025-08-08; date approximate).

items.summary: The tracker argued the slowdown is temporary: once post-training scales up, the developer's next flagship will probably use more compute than its Feb-2025 model, returning to the ~5x/yr growth trend for the most compute-intensive runs.
items.detail: Epoch Gradient Update 'Why GPT-5 used less training compute than GPT-4.5 (but GPT-6 probably won't)' (late Sept 2025; date approximate).

items.summary: Late-2025 flagships from two other Bloc A developers had no public compute estimate, so the 'largest known run' may understate the true frontier.
items.detail: Epoch entries for Gemini 3 Pro (2025-11-18, compute unknown) and Claude Opus 4.5 (2025-11-24, 'very likely >1e25').
